title: Wearable Patch for Atrial Fibrillation Detection With On-Device Inference
problem: Continuous electrocardiogram monitoring produces large data volumes that drain wearable batteries when streamed, while simple threshold detectors give many false alarms during motion.
solution: A skin patch records single-lead electrocardiogram and accelerometer signals. A small neural network running on the patch microcontroller classifies each thirty second window, using the accelerometer to gate windows corrupted by motion. Only windows classified as irregular are compressed and transmitted to a phone, together with a confidence value.

elements.text: A skin patch with electrodes recording a single-lead electrocardiogram signal
An accelerometer in the patch that produces a motion signal
A neural network executed on a microcontroller of the patch that classifies fixed-length signal windows as regular or irregular rhythm
Gating of windows by the motion signal so that motion-corrupted windows are not classified
Compression and wireless transmission of only the windows classified as irregular
Transmission of a classification confidence value with each transmitted window

dependent_features: The network is quantised to eight bits
The patch enters a low power mode between windows
